The next account then sees every follow-up question on an empty draft. The core already owns `submitted`, `resetForm` and `handleTypeChange`, so this state belongs there. Moving it also deletes both copies and the wrapper lambdas.

**[P2] Remove the inherited bearer credential too.** When the orchestrator shell has `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` set, local workers retain it through `githubEnvironment` and this filter, and Claude selects it ahead of the dedicated directory's subscription sign-in. This lets workers use the orchestrator's credential despite `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at the worker account.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Inherited bearer token bypasses worker account selection

## Affected sites
- `tools/lib/orchestrator-config.mjs:197,218-222`: the filter deletes only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
- `tools/lib/github-auth.mjs:34-38`: local launches copy the parent environment, preserving `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- `tools/launch-worker.mjs:380-384`: that environment reaches the worker gate and its Claude child.

## Evidence
A direct synthetic call to `workerAccountEnvironment` retained `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` unchanged. The exact CLI version cited by this PR independently confirms that it selects this credential even with an empty config directory:

```sh
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="<temporary-home>" CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="<empty-worker-config-directory>" ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=synthetic-review-token npm exec --yes --package=@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.318 -- claude auth status
```

Complete JSON response, with directory values replaced:

```json
{
  "loggedIn": true,
  "authMethod": "oauth_token",
  "apiProvider": "firstParty",
  "analyticsDisabled": false,
  "projectsDirectory": "<empty-worker-config-directory>/projects",
  "configDirectory": "<empty-worker-config-directory>",
  "loginExpiresAt": null
}
```

Without `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, the same invocation returned the same key set with `loggedIn: false` and `authMethod: "none"`, and exited 1. No model request or real credential was used. [P2] Retain incomplete-content evidence before classifying mail
````

Gmail can store a text MIME part behind `body.attachmentId` instead of inline `body.data`; this traversal silently drops that content and its identifier. A message with inline thanks and an externally stored complaint or refund request therefore reaches classification as thanks only, with no indication that content is missing, yet can still pass the automatic-send policy.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown

- `tools/orbit-mail.mjs:25-26,47-50`: only inline data becomes a body, and no omitted-part metadata is saved.
- `tools/lib/auto-work-google.mjs:42,52-55`: the client has no attachment-body retrieval operation.
- `.claude/skills/auto-work/SKILL.md:134-147`: mixed concerns must remain drafts and classification must use the whole message.

## Required outcome
- Retrieve externally stored message text before automatic classification, or retain an explicit incomplete-content condition that prevents automatic sends until the content has been reviewed.
- Cover a message with both inline text and an attachmentId-backed text part; it must not silently become eligible for an automatic thanks reply.

## Evidence
- Google's MessagePartBody contract states that data may be empty when body content is sent as a separate attachment, and that attachmentId must be retrieved with messages.attachments.get.
- Reproduced collection of such a message: only the inline body survived, the external part ID was absent from the pending item, and replyToMail accepted a simple praise receipt and sent.
````

[P2] Fence the predecessor when owner adoption transfers the run

This transfer records the predecessor only in `ownerHandoff` and clears `relay.from`, so the existing superseded-session guard does not recognize the old session as superseded. If that terminal resumes, it can overwrite the successor's newer intake, including `sendAttempted` protection against duplicate replies; this reproduces both with and without an earlier context-relay chain.
